analysis.reason: This paper presents the first direct observational identification of common-envelope evolution (CEE) orbital inspiral and merger in M31 (AT 2025abao), directly revealing ejecta-CSM shock interaction and plateau energetics relevant to high-energy transient physics.
analysis.result: AT 2025abao is an AGB-star common-envelope merger ($M_1 \approx 7\,M_\odot$, $M_2 \approx 0.7\,M_\odot$, $q \approx 0.10_{-0.05}^{+0.10}$) exhibiting an optical eruption with peak luminosity $L \approx 2.5 \times 10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$, an $\approx 80\,\mathrm{d}$ plateau, and ejecta-CSM shock interaction with $v_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}$ decelerating from $\approx 900\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ to $\approx 150\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ matching $\rho(r) \propto r^{-2}$. The orbital dissipation energy $\Delta E_{\rm orb} \approx 10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg}$ predominantly drives kinetic ejection ($KE_{\rm ej} \sim 10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg}$ for $M_{\rm ej} \approx 0.1\text{--}0.2\,M_\odot$) rather than binding energy unbinding ($E_{\rm unbind} \approx 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg}$) or radiation ($E_{\rm rad} \approx 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg}$), governed by $\Delta E_{\rm orb} = E_{\rm unbind} + E_{\rm rad} + KE_{\rm ej}$.

analysis.problem: Direct observational verification of binary common envelope evolution (CEE) dynamics, specifically how orbital energy is dissipated by drag during inspiral and whether envelope unbinding or kinetic ejection dominates the energy sink.
analysis.method: Multiband photometric monitoring (ZTF, WINTER, WIRC, Cerberus high-cadence SDSS-$r$ with $1\,\mathrm{s}$ sampling), Swift UVOT/XRT, SPHEREx ($0.7\text{--}5\,\mu\mathrm{m}$), and JWST/MIRI SED modeling. Progenitor quiescent mass loss is modeled via $\dot{M} = \eta_{\rm gd}\frac{4\pi v_{\rm wind}R_{\rm in}\tau_V}{\kappa_V} \sim 10^{-5}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$, and precursor drag dissipation is quantified by $L_{\rm decay} = 4\pi G^{3/2}C_d M_2^2 \rho a^{1/2}(M_1+M_2)^{-1/2} \propto a^{-5/2} \approx 3\times 10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with MESA envelope binding energy $E_{\rm bind}(>m) = \int_m^{M_\star}\left(-\frac{Gm_r}{r}+u\right)\mathrm{d}m$.
assumptions: Circumstellar material follows a wind-like density profile $\rho(r) \propto r^{-2}$ with momentum-conserving shock interaction.
limits: Available optical/NIR spectra cannot definitively exclude an ultra-tight surviving binary without future infrared dust tracking or strict constraints on residual mechanical power $\dot{E} < 10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$.

figures.caption: Figure 10: A graphical representation of the different phases of AT 2025abao. a) The quiescent binary system comprising a $\approx 7$ M ⊙ AGB and a $\approx 0.7$ M ⊙ star, surrounded by an extended dust shell from mass loss from the binary following Roche Lobe overflow of the primary. b) The precursor brightening phase that began in 2018, marking the onset of CEE, powered by frictional drag on the inspiraling companion lasting for $\approx 7$ years. analysis.reason: This paper develops a dimension-free, problem-independent adaptive mesh refinement criterion based on a higher-order ($N=4$) smoothness indicator for Newtonian, SRMHD, and GRMHD simulations. It provides valuable numerical methodology improvements for simulating relativistic blast waves, magnetohydrodynamic instabilities, and black hole accretion flows (SANE/MAD) relevant to high-energy central engines.
analysis.result: The AMR criterion achieves runtime speedups of $1.45\times - 3.66\times$ across Newtonian and SRMHD benchmarks: in the Shu–Osher test, MeshBlock cycles decrease by $4.26\times$ with a $1.72\times$ speedup; in SRMHD magnetic rotor tests, MeshBlock cycles are reduced by $3.4\times$ with a $2.8\times$ speedup at an effective resolution of $1536^2$. In GRMHD Kerr black hole accretion simulations with spin $a/M_{\rm BH}=0.9$, the algorithm tracks turbulent MRI accretion streams and outflows in SANE ($W_{\rm max}=20$, base grid $96^3$) and successfully resolves magnetic flux eruption dynamics in MAD where the horizon dimensionless flux reaches $\phi_{\rm BH} = \Phi_{\rm BH} / \sqrt{\dot{M}} \gtrsim 15$.
analysis.problem: Traditional curvature-based AMR refinement criteria, such as the Löhner-type indicator, rely heavily on empirical threshold tuning and problem-dependent choice of variables, making them difficult to generalize across multi-scale relativistic MHD problems and black hole accretion environments without incurring excessive computational overhead.
analysis.method: The algorithm computes the undivided fourth-order difference on a symmetric 5-point stencil ($N=4$), $\Delta^{(4)}u \equiv u_{i+2}-4u_{i+1}+6u_i-4u_{i-1}+u_{i-2}$, to define a local dimensionless oscillation measure $e_i = |\Delta^{(4)}u| / (|u_i| + \delta)$. Cells are refined when $e_i > 4^{-2} = 0.0625$, kept unchanged within $[4^{-3}, 4^{-2}]$, and coarsened when $e_i < 4^{-3} = 0.015625$. In multi-dimensional MHD implemented in AthenaK, the criterion evaluates conserved variables $(D, M^j, E, B^j)$ along all axes, automatically coarsening cells below the rest-mass density floor $D_{\boldsymbol{i}} \le D_{\mathrm{floor}}$ and using smoothing parameters $\epsilon_{\mathrm{mom}} \sim D_{\mathrm{floor}} U$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{B}} \sim (D_{\mathrm{floor}} U^2)^{1/2}$ to prevent division by zero.
limits: Failing to resolve initial discontinuities at the finest grid level causes staircasing artifacts that are nonlinearly amplified, requiring pre-evolution multi-level AMR initialization.

analysis.reason: This work connects massive binary population synthesis with semi-analytical radio hypernebula models to characterize the demographics of super-Eddington accretion systems and evaluate their role as persistent radio sources (PRSs) associated with FRBs and LFBOTs.
analysis.result: The dominant binary mass-transfer channels driving super-Eddington accretion are $\mathrm{HG}\rightarrow\mathrm{HeMS}$ ($\sim 41\%$) and $\mathrm{HeHG}\rightarrow\mathrm{WD}$ ($\sim 33\%$), governed by an anti-correlation scaling relation $\dot{m}^{1.25\pm 0.05}\sim 10^{5.33\pm 0.23}\left(\frac{t_{\rm acc}}{10^{3}\,{\rm yr}}\right)^{-1}$ across mass-transfer rates $\dot{m}\equiv \dot{M}/\dot{M}_{\rm Edd}\sim 10^{2-7}$ and durations $t_{\rm acc}\sim 10^{0-6}\,{\rm yr}$. The local formation rate of these systems is $\mathcal{R}\sim 10^{3}\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$. The resulting radio hypernebulae exhibit peak spectral luminosities of $L_{\nu,\rm peak}\sim 10^{28-30}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$ at $1.4-3\,{\rm GHz}$, with maximal nebular emission produced by intermediate parameters ($t_{\rm acc}\sim 10^{2-3}\,{\rm yr}$, $\dot{m}\sim 10^{5-6}$). Tens of hypernebulae have angular sizes $\theta\approx 2R_{\rm n}(t_{\rm peak})/D_{\rm A}\gtrsim 10\,{\rm mas}$ resolvable by VLBI at $D_{\rm A}\sim 100\,{\rm Mpc}$ with spatial offsets $\phi\approx v_{\rm sys}t_{\rm SN1\to HNb}/D_{\rm A}\sim 1''-10''$ induced by natal kicks ($v_{\rm sys}\sim 10-20\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$). In DSA-2000, radio precursor emission could be detected for $\sim 1\%$ of LFBOTs out to $\sim 1\,{\rm Gpc}$.
analysis.problem: Current empirical samples of super-Eddington accretors (such as local ULXs and microquasars like SS 433) are heavily biased toward long-lived, stable systems, leaving the event rates, radio emission, and transient associations of short-lived ($t_{\rm acc}\sim 10^{0-6}\,{\rm yr}$) extreme mass-transfer episodes poorly constrained across cosmic time.
analysis.method: Combines binary population synthesis with COMPAS (v02.35.03) with the semi-analytical hypernebula model of Sridhar & Metzger (2022). Stable Roche-lobe overflow mass transfer is dictated by thermal timescales $\dot{M}_{\rm th} = \frac{M_{\rm d,env}}{\tau_{\rm KH}} = \frac{R_{\rm d}L_{\rm d}}{GM_{\rm d}}$, while unstable transfers follow the $\alpha_{\rm CE}-\lambda$ energy formalism. The accretion flow powers a quasi-spherical wind ($v_{\rm w}\approx 0.03c$) with kinetic power $L_{\rm w}\simeq \frac{1}{2}\dot{M}v_{\rm w}^2$ and a mildly relativistic jet ($v_{\rm j}\approx 0.1-0.3c$) carrying kinetic power $L_{\rm j}=\eta L_{\rm w}$ with efficiency $\eta\sim 0.1$. Relativistic electrons are heated at the jet termination shock with efficiency $\varepsilon_{\rm e}\sim 0.1-0.5$ into a relativistic Maxwellian distribution with mean Lorentz factor $\bar{\gamma}\approx \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_{\rm e}\frac{m_{\rm p}}{m_{\rm e}}\frac{v_{\rm j}^2}{c^2}$ and inject synchrotron radiation into a magnetized bubble (magnetization $\sigma_{\rm j}\sim 0.1$) expanding into the CSM ($n_{\rm csm}=10\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$).
assumptions: COMPAS limits the mass growth rate of accreting compact objects to the Eddington rate.
limits: The adopted parameter grid is not unique because the hypernebula model contains substantial uncertainties in both physical assumptions and parameter selections.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates the multimode gravitational wave imprint and energy redistribution of tilted accretion disks around spinning Kerr black holes using 3D GRMHD and Teukolsky formalisms. analysis.result: During disk alignment over $10000M \leq t \leq 30000M$, the tilt angle decreases from $69.3^{\circ}$ to $13.9^{\circ}$ (reaching $\sim 9^{\circ}$ at $t=45000M$), while the gravitational wave energy fraction in higher-order modes $R_{\geq 3}$ decreases from $0.042$ to $0.011$ (reaching $0.007$ at $t=45000M$). The mode energy distribution follows the Wigner small $d$-matrix transformation $h_{\ell m}^{\rm geom}(t) = e^{-i m \phi_d} d^\ell_{m 0}(\theta_d) h_{\ell 0}^{\rm d}(t)$ with power allocation $p_{\ell m} = |d^\ell_{m 0}(\theta_d)|^2$.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates the turbulent magnetized interstellar medium and statistical depolarization in the Small Magellanic Cloud using background polarized radio sources from the ASKAP POSSUM survey. It has no substantive connection to the group's research focus on high-energy transients (such as FRBs/PRS, supernova central engines, shock breakout, CSM interaction, relativistic jets, or compact object high-energy observations).
analysis.result: Using ASKAP POSSUM Pilot II observations, the authors find that the fraction of polarized background sources on-SMC ($N_{\mathrm{H\,I}} > 2\times 10^{21}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-2}$) is significantly suppressed to $f_{\mathrm{pol,on}} = 0.227 \pm 0.021$ relative to off-SMC sightlines ($f_{\mathrm{pol,off}} = 0.360 \pm 0.015$), anti-correlating with Faraday dispersion which peaks up to $\Sigma_{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}} = 108.8\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$ ($5.0\,\sigma_{\mathrm{null}}$ excess). Fitting Burn's external Faraday dispersion law $p_{\mathrm{peak}} = p_0 \exp(-2\sigma_\phi^2 \langle\lambda^4\rangle)$ with $\sigma_\phi = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ yields $k = 0.32\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}\ pc^{-1/2}\ cm^3}$, constraining the sub-beam random magnetic field to $B_r = (1.0 \pm 0.2)(l_0 / 0.5\ \mathrm{pc})^{-1/2}\ \mu\mathrm{G}$. For cell size $l_0 \lesssim 6\ \mathrm{pc}$, this requires $B_r \gtrsim 0.3\ \mu\mathrm{G}$ and implies a steep magnetic energy spectrum (slope $\approx -2$) between $6\ \mathrm{pc}$ and $160\ \mathrm{pc}$.
analysis.problem: Investigating how the turbulent, magnetized interstellar medium (ISM) in the low-metallicity, tidally disturbed Small Magellanic Cloud causes beam depolarization and Faraday depth dispersion $\Sigma_{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}}$ of background radio sources on parsec and sub-parsec scales.
analysis.method: Analysis of ASKAP POSSUM observations convolved to $21^{\prime\prime} \approx 6\ \mathrm{pc}$ resolution with diffuse polarized emission subtracted via annulus median filtering; RM-synthesis across $\phi \in [-6000, 6000]\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$ and Stokes $QU$-fitting; statistical depolarization mapping on equal-area grids ($2.25\ \mathrm{deg}^2$) using polarized fraction $f_{\mathrm{pol}} = N_{\mathrm{pol}}/N_{\mathrm{tot}}$ and peak Faraday depth dispersion $\Sigma_{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}} = \sqrt{\sum(\phi_{\mathrm{peak}} - \overline{\phi_{\mathrm{peak}}})^2 / (N_{\mathrm{pol}}-1)}\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}}$; Burn depolarization modeling $\sigma_\phi = k\sqrt{\mathrm{EM}}$ with $k = 0.812 B_r \sqrt{l_0/3}\ \mathrm{rad\ m^{-2}\ pc^{-1/2}\ cm^3}$.
assumptions: Depolarization is predominantly driven by random-walk fluctuations of tangled turbulent magnetic fields $B_r$ on sub-beam scales rather than large-scale thermal electron density fluctuations.
limits: Translating the depolarization parameter $k$ into an absolute magnetic field strength requires knowledge of the unknown turbulent cell correlation size $l_0$ and SMC 3D line-of-sight depth geometry.

For an FRB volumetric rate $\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB} = 7.3 \times 10^4\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the required birth rate satisfies $\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm birth}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm mag}} \sim 0.1\left(\frac{\mathcal{R}_{\rm FRB}}{\mathcal{R}_{\rm CCSN}}\right)\left(\frac{0.1}{f_{\rm b}}\right)\left(\frac{0.4}{f_{\rm mag}}\right)\left(\frac{100\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}}{\bar{r}}\right)$.

analysis.problem: Whether repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources maintain stationary burst rates indefinitely or cease activity within months to years as predicted by magnetar central engine models.
analysis.method: Formulates an unseen-species estimation framework utilizing Robbins formula $n^{\rm pred}_k = (k+1) N_{k+1} \frac{T_B}{T_A}$ across time windows of length $W = 180\ \mathrm{d}$ separated by gap $\Delta$, evaluating the gap statistic $R(\Delta) = \frac{\sum_s \sum_{k=1}^3 n^{\rm obs}_k(s)}{\sum_s \sum_{k=1}^3 t(s)(k+1)N_{k+1}(s)}$ and decay ratio $S = \frac{R(\Delta \geq 360\ \mathrm{d})}{R(\Delta \leq 90\ \mathrm{d})}$, with exposure calibrated via the Good–Toulmin estimator $N_{\rm new} = \sum_{k \geq 1} (-1)^{k+1} t^k N_k$.
assumptions: Each source is initially assumed to emit bursts following a steady Poisson process with constant mean rate $r$ drawn from rate distribution $f(r)$.
limits: The statistical measurement directly applies only to repeating sources, whereas truly one-off events enter neither observed counts nor predictions.

analysis.reason: SN 2025wiu provides exceptional multi-band photometric and spectroscopic coverage of an extraordinary Type Ib supernova with a post-maximum bump, providing quantitative constraints on shock cooling, central engine activity, and circumstellar medium interaction.
analysis.result: SN 2025wiu displays peak absolute magnitudes of $M_u = -17.5\pm 0.1$, $M_g = -18.11\pm 0.01$, and $M_r = -18.24\pm 0.04\,\mathrm{mag}$, accompanied by early shock cooling from a compact progenitor with $R_\star \approx 4\,R_\odot$, $M_{\mathrm{ej}} \approx 2\,M_\odot$, and $E \approx 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$. At $\sim 50\,\mathrm{days}$ post-maximum, it develops a secondary bump peaking at $L_{\mathrm{peak}} \sim 2.4\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with total radiated energy $E_{\mathrm{bump}} \sim 10^{49}\,\mathrm{erg}$ and duration $\Delta t \approx 42\,\mathrm{days}$. Synthesized $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ mass estimated from the primary peak via Arnett's rule is $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} \approx 0.47\,M_\odot$, contrasting sharply with late-time radioactive tail deposition ($f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1 - \exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$ with $T_0 = 173^{+44}_{-41}\,\mathrm{days}$) which yields $M_{\mathrm{Ni}} = 0.13^{+0.05}_{-0.02}\,M_\odot$. The bump energy implies an interacting CSM mass of $M_{\mathrm{CSM}} \sim 0.03\,M_\odot$ at radius $R \sim 5\times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{cm}$.

analysis.problem: Investigating whether the high peak luminosity and prominent post-maximum bump of the slowly evolving Type Ib supernova SN 2025wiu can be reconciled with standard radioactive decay, or whether delayed circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction, magnetar spin-down, fallback accretion, or a double-$^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ distribution is required.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch optical and NIR photometry combined with optical spectroscopy, analytical $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ radioactive decay modeling via the Arnett rule and deposition function $f_{\mathrm{dep}}(t) = 1 - \exp[-(T_0/t)^2]$, photon diffusion timescale constraints ($t_{\mathrm{d}} = \sqrt{3\kappa M_{\mathrm{ej}} / (4\pi v_{\mathrm{ej}} c)}$), shock cooling emission modeling, and semi-analytical decomposed light-curve fitting involving CSM interaction and magnetar spin-down models.
assumptions: Circumstellar medium interaction converts kinetic energy to radiation with efficiency $\eta = 0.5$ at relative ejecta-CSM velocity $v_{\mathrm{rel}} \approx 8000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$
limits: Persistently weak spectral line features and absence of narrow emission lines up to $\sim 110\,\mathrm{days}$ post-maximum limit direct spectroscopic detection of unshocked circumstellar material

analysis.reason: This paper investigates the dual gamma-ray components of middle-aged SNR IC 443 detected by LHAASO, modeling hadronic emission from SNR-molecular cloud interactions and leptonic emission from the associated PWN, providing direct constraints on Galactic cosmic-ray acceleration and TeV halo formation.
analysis.result: For compact component C0, the SNR-MC hadronic model reproduces the observed SED with a clear $\pi^0$-decay peak, yielding a proton injection spectral index $s = 2.03$, diffusion suppression factor $\chi = 0.08$, and momentum cutoff $p_{\rm cut} = 5.0\times 10^5\text{ GeV}/c$, confirming C0 as a potential Galactic PeVatron candidate. For extended component C1, leptonic inverse Compton scattering from PWN CXOU J061705.3+222127 electrons reproduces the emission with spin-down luminosity $L_{\rm age} = 1.0\times 10^{36}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$, magnetic field $B_{\rm age} = 4.7\ \mu\text{G}$, electron injection index $s = 1.90$, and energy cutoff $E_{\rm cut} = 1.75\times 10^5\text{ GeV}$, requiring strongly suppressed diffusion $D_1 = 1\times 10^{26}\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$ with Bohm scaling $\delta = 1$, identifying C1 as a candidate TeV halo.
analysis.problem: Disentangling the distinct physical origins and radiation mechanisms of the compact component C0 and the extended component C1 (angular scale $\sim 0.67^\circ$) in the middle-aged supernova remnant IC 443.
analysis.method: The authors apply two independent transport and emission models: (1) An SNR-MC hadronic model for C0 accounting for diffusive shock acceleration and energy-dependent proton escape with spectrum $N_{\rm esc}(p) = N_0 p_{\rm br,1}^{-\beta/\alpha} p^{-s}$ ($p \le p_{\rm br,1}$) and $N_0 p^{-(s+\beta/\alpha)} \exp(-p/p_{\rm cut})$ ($p > p_{\rm br,1}$), integrated over a molecular cloud shell $F(p) = \eta \int_{L_1}^{L_2} f(t_{\rm age}, r, p) 4\pi r^2 dr$ with $\beta = 3(3-s)/2$ and $\alpha = 6.5$. (2) A spherically symmetric multi-zone leptonic Fokker-Planck transport model for C1 incorporating spatial diffusion $D(p) = 10^{28}\chi (cp/10\text{ GeV})^\delta\text{ cm}^2\text{ s}^{-1}$, advection, and radiative cooling $\dot{E}_{e,\rm rad} = \frac{4}{3}\sigma_{\rm T} c \left(\frac{E_e}{m_e c^2}\right)^2 [U_B + U_{\rm rad}]$ from the central pulsar wind nebula.

analysis.reason: This work presents 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer simulations of the kilonova AT2017gfo, demonstrating that mass scaling and velocity compression of dynamical ejecta self-consistently reproduce the bolometric light curve and early multi-epoch spectra without requiring an ad hoc separate lanthanide-poor component.
analysis.result: By scaling the ejecta mass to $M = 0.04\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ and halving expansion velocities (with half the mass concentrated at radial velocities $v_{r} \lesssim 0.09c$ and peak density at $0.04c$), the 3D model reproduces the bolometric luminosity and optical-to-NIR spectra of AT2017gfo at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$, $2.4\,\mathrm{d}$, and $3.4\,\mathrm{d}$ across $5500\text{--}15\,000\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. The reduced velocity compresses the ejecta density, raising the $\gamma$-ray thermalization efficiency at $1.4\,\mathrm{d}$ from $\sim 0.3$ to $\sim 0.55$ and boosting deposited power by $\sim 30\%$ at $1\text{--}4\,\mathrm{d}$. Through the effective temperature scaling $T_{\mathrm{eff}} \propto L^{1/4}(v_{\mathrm{ph}}t)^{-1/2}$, smaller photospheric radii $R_{\mathrm{ph}} = v_{\mathrm{ph}}t$ maintain higher photospheric temperatures and avoid premature reddening. Key spectroscopic identifications include: $\mathrm{Sr\ II}\ \lambda\lambda 10037, 10327, 10915$ generating the $\sim 10\,500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ NIR peak; $\mathrm{Y\ II}\ \lambda 7882$ contributing to the $\sim 7300\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ peak; $\mathrm{La\ III}\ \lambda\lambda 13894, 14096$ and $\mathrm{Gd\ III}\ \lambda 14333$ forming the $\sim 13\,500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ shoulder; and $\mathrm{Sr\ II}\ \lambda 4216$ creating the blue flux cutoff at $\lesssim 4500\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$. In contrast, 2D azimuthally averaged models are dimmer by a factor of $\sim 3$ at $\sim 1\,\mathrm{d}$ because azimuthal averaging artificially mixes lanthanide-poor channels ($X_{\mathrm{lan}} < 10^{-3}$) with high-opacity lanthanides.
analysis.problem: First-principles numerical relativity simulations yield 3D dynamical ejecta with masses ($M \approx 0.005\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$) and expansion velocities ($v_{\mathrm{max}} \approx 0.48c$) that are too low in mass and too high in speed compared to empirical AT2017gfo inferences ($M \approx 0.03\text{--}0.05\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$), causing synthesized light curves to decay prematurely and spectra to peak at overly red or Doppler-shifted wavelengths; furthermore, whether a physically distinct, unmixed lanthanide-poor component is strictly needed to explain the early blue emission remains unresolved.
analysis.method: Multi-dimensional time-dependent Monte Carlo radiative transfer code ARTIS applied to a 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) binary neutron star merger model ($2 \times 1.35\,\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$, SFHo equation of state) mapped at $t_{\mathrm{snap}} = 0.1\,\mathrm{d}$. Bound-bound transitions ($4.9 \times 10^{7}$ transitions across 83 elements, $Z=57\text{--}70$ in AD3) are computed under local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). Radiative transfer is evaluated across line-by-line (LBL) Sobolev optical depths $\tau_i$, expansion opacities $\kappa_{\mathrm{exp}} = \frac{1}{ct\rho}\sum_i \frac{\lambda_i}{\Delta\lambda}(1 - e^{-\tau_i})$, and capped line-binned opacities with optical depth threshold $\tau_{\mathrm{l,max}}$ where bin optical depth is $\tau_{\mathrm{bin}} = \sum_i \min(\tau_i, \tau_{\mathrm{l,max}})$ and transmission probability $P_0 = e^{-\tau_{\mathrm{bin}}}$.
assumptions: All radiative transfer calculations assume local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) at every timestep to compute level populations and ionization fractions via the Saha and Boltzmann relations.
limits: The uniform velocity compression factor ($v \to v/2$) serves as an empirical proxy for slower post-merger accretion disk wind outflows rather than a dynamically consistent hydrodynamical simulation.

analysis.reason: This work presents the first infrared spectroscopic investigation and wind radiative transfer modeling of Pa30, the bound compact remnant of the Type Iax supernova SN 1181. It provides key empirical wind parameters and ionization constraints directly relevant to surviving central engines of deflagration supernovae.
analysis.result: The infrared spectrum of Pa30's central star is modeled by a non-LTE stellar wind with luminosity $L = 3.6 \times 10^4\,L_{\odot}$ ($10^{4.6}\,L_\odot$), effective radius $R_{*}(\tau=2.3) = 0.136\,R_{\odot}$, mass-loss rate $\dot{M} = 2.0 \times 10^{-6}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, and terminal wind velocity $V_{\infty} \sim 15{,}000\text{--}16{,}000\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in a C/O/Ne-dominated atmosphere ($Y_{\mathrm{O}}=0.41, Y_{\mathrm{Ne}}=0.44, Y_{\mathrm{C}}=0.13$). The near-infrared emission is dominated by hydrogenic $\mathrm{O\,VI}$ transitions ($n \rightarrow n-1$), including a $1.12\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ P Cygni profile ($3p\,^2\mathrm{P}^o - 3d\,^2\mathrm{D}$), where dielectronic recombination of $\mathrm{O\,V}$ at $T \sim 20{,}000\,\mathrm{K}$ with rate coefficient $\alpha_{\mathrm{dr}} \approx 3 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{cm}^3\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ dominates radiative recombination ($\alpha_{\mathrm{rr}} \approx 3 \times 10^{-12}\,\mathrm{cm}^3\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$). High-ionization emission lines are successfully reproduced by a collisionally ionized coronal plasma model.

analysis.method: Combined space-based spectroscopy from SPHEREx ($0.75\text{--}5.0\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, $R \sim 35\text{--}41$) with high-resolution ground-based NIR spectra from Gemini North GNIRS ($R \sim 1{,}200$), TNG NICS ($R = 500$), and DOT TANSPEC ($R \sim 1{,}600$).
